title: Loss and gradient descent
summary: See how repeated small updates can improve a prediction.

sections.title: Turn an error into an objective
paragraphs: For a prediction y_hat and target y, squared error is (y_hat - y) squared. Averaging it over examples gives mean squared error. Squaring penalizes large misses more strongly and makes positive and negative errors contribute positively.

For the simple model y_hat = weight times x, the derivative of squared error with respect to weight is 2 times x times (weight times x minus y). The derivative describes the local direction and rate of loss change, not the best possible final weight.

sections.title: Update carefully
paragraphs: Gradient descent subtracts a learning rate times the derivative from each parameter. Too small a learning rate can make progress slow; too large can overshoot or diverge. A decreasing training loss does not prove good generalization.
Check a baseline, inspect the loss curve, and evaluate unseen examples. Feature scale affects the gradients, so a learning rate that works for inputs near 1 can fail when inputs are near 10,000.

code.source:
xs, ys = [1., 2., 3.], [2., 4., 6.]
weight, rate = 0., 0.05
for step in range(60):
    gradient = sum(2*x*(weight*x-y) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)) / len(xs)
    weight -= rate * gradient
loss = sum((weight*x-y)**2 for x, y in zip(xs, ys)) / len(xs)
print("Weight:", round(weight, 4), "Loss:", round(loss, 8))
print("Prediction for 4:", round(weight * 4, 3))
code.explanation: The dataset follows exactly y = 2x, so a weight close to 2 is expected. Real data usually contains noise and may not follow a straight line.

steps: Record the final weight and loss.
Explain why a larger step can move away from the solution.
practice.solution: With this feature scale, 0.05 converges rapidly, 0.005 moves more slowly, and 0.3 overshoots repeatedly. Compare loss rather than assuming more aggressive updates are better.
practice.expected: The original weight approaches 2 and the prediction for 4 approaches 8.

quiz.question: What does a falling training loss establish?
options: The model is guaranteed to work on new data
The objective is improving on the training examples
quiz.explanation: The optimization objective can improve even while the model overfits or learns from flawed labels.
